post.title: Why does your iPhone give Wi-Fi a fake address?
post.caption:
Why does your iPhone give Wi-Fi a fake address? 📶

Every device has a hardware MAC address it uses to talk to Wi-Fi. If it showed the same one everywhere, network operators and anyone watching could link your visits and build a trail of where you go. So your iPhone uses a private Wi-Fi address: a different one for each network. On iOS 18 and later, networks with WPA2 or stronger security get a Fixed one, while open or weak-security networks get a Rotating one that changes every two weeks. Check it in Settings, Wi-Fi, tap the info button next to a network, Private Wi-Fi Address. Turn it off only if a network won't work with it.
Send this to someone who joins every café Wi-Fi.
keywords: why does my iphone change its mac address

sources.note: Apple, Use private Wi-Fi addresses on Apple devices: a device identifies itself to each network with a different Wi-Fi (MAC) address; the same address across all networks lets operators and observers relate it to your activity and location over time; Fixed is the default on WPA2 or stronger networks, Rotating (a new private address every 2 weeks) on weak or no security (iOS 18+)
Apple Platform Security, Wi-Fi privacy: randomized MAC addresses for Wi-Fi scans when not associated, so the address can't be used to persistently track a device by passive observers
